clue.text: Celebrity coming from nowhere, now nobody

indicators.note: coming from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A star who rose from obscurity is now a has-been.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrity in the sense of fame: both name the state of being widely known and acclaimed.

clue.text: Ancient Italian six-footer briefly charming

parts.note: a Roman was a citizen of ancient Rome

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: a tick in its larval stage has six legs, so it is a six-footer

explanation.surface: An old Roman, tall and abrupt but appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person but means a six-legged creature; larval ticks have six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that evokes love or idealised feeling is charming in a dreamy, sentimental way.

clue.text: Short chap coming up with unfinished article — from this direction?

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue means the piece is written bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: Ron is a short form of a man's name such as Ronald

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A small man arrives with a half-written piece, and someone asks where he came from.
explanation.walkthrough: Wind is named for where it blows from, so the cold wind comes from this direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass point names the direction from which, say, a wind blows: up on most maps.

clue.text: Old rare metal detected in animals

definitions.text: Old rare metal detected in animals

parts.words: Old rare metal detected in animals
parts.note: the metal's old name is literally two creatures put together, a canine predator then a male sheep, so it can be found in animals

explanation.surface: A precious ancient metal found inside creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: No indicator builds it: the whole clue hints that the metal's name splits into two beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: An older name for tungsten, a dense rare metallic element.

clue.text: Line in answer penned by Boris, strangely

indicators.note: penned by means held inside, as in an animal pen, so one piece goes within the other
strangely says the letters of Boris come out in an odd new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A sentence in a reply written oddly by a politician named Boris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' turns BORIS into ISOBR, and 'penned by' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather-map line joining points of equal atmospheric pressure is a specific kind of line.

clue.text: Ten sung about weapon

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are moved around into another order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A choir of ten singing about a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A light British submachine gun of the Second World War is a firearm.

clue.text: Some sense in this, perhaps: finding undergarment in small room

parts.note: a bra is an item of underwear
a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery

explanation.surface: Finding underwear in a prison room, which might take some sense to explain.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is by example: a unit of the grey matter might hold some sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A neuron of the brain is jokingly where intelligence or common sense resides.

clue.text: Food right on a plate

parts.note: a dish is a plate

explanation.surface: Food served right there on a plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A pungent red root vegetable eaten in salads is a food.

clue.text: Bull and mare desperate for shelter

indicators.note: desperate suggests wild, frantic behaviour, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Two farm animals in a storm frantic to find cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' simply joins the two animals; only BULL and MARE are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A brolly is a portable shelter from rain, and the word also means a protective cover in general.

clue.text: Poor satire upset one, from experience

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters fall into another order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A weak satire offended someone who knew better from experience.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin phrase for reasoning that proceeds from observed facts, i.e. knowledge drawn from experience.

clue.text: Antelopes from eastern districts

parts.note: lands means regions or districts

explanation.surface: Wild animals sourced from the eastern regions.
explanation.definitionFit: Large African antelopes with spiralled horns; the plural matches the plural definition.

clue.text: Creep from Altrincham

indicators.note: from here means some letters are taken out of the town name that follows

explanation.surface: A sneaky person who comes from Altrincham, a town near Manchester in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creep' is the verb, to move slowly, not the unpleasant person the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To move forward a tiny distance at a time is to creep along slowly.

clue.text: Sort out again, finding nothing in tangled earrings by middle of bed

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the jumbled jewellery
tangled says the letters of earrings are knotted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
O is the round figure zero, nothing

indicators.note: middle of picks the central letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Tidying a messy jewellery box: knotted earrings found empty beside the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tangled' makes REGRANIS from EARRINGS; 'in' puts O inside it, and 'middle of' bed gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearrange or restructure something is to arrange it once more, i.e. to sort it out again.

clue.text: Event about cats and mice run badly

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: badly says the following letters are put together in a mangled order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A domestic incident involving cats and mice that goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' shuffles CATS and MICE RUN into IRCUMSTANCE; 'and' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A happening or fact surrounding a situation can be called an occurrence or event.

clue.text: Trim spliff in dodgy nightclub

parts.note: to clip is to trim
a spliff is a cannabis cigarette, also called a joint

explanation.surface: Someone trimming a cannabis cigarette in a seedy club.
explanation.definitionFit: A club that overcharges or swindles its customers is a disreputable nightspot.

clue.text: You may find this on your shoulders, end of beard and collar

definitions.text: You may find this on your shoulders

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a ruff is a frilled Elizabethan collar

explanation.surface: Something found on the shoulders near a beard and a collar.
explanation.definitionFit: Flakes of dead skin from the scalp often land on the shoulders of dark clothing.

clue.text: Bury lass on front of rocket — for such a space journey?

parts.note: inter means to bury a body
Stella is a girl's name, a lass

indicators.note: front of picks the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An odd instruction to bury a girl on the nose cone of a rocket.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description by example: a journey of this type would be between the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Travel between stars is the adjective that describes such a long trip through space.

clue.text: I let cat out — that's touching

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are let loose and come back in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Releasing the cat is a heart-warming gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touching' looks like moving, but means relating to touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the sense of touch or perceptible by feel is a physical sense of touching.

clue.text: Do something audacious: see if this thing fits

definitions.meaning: an idiom for chancing your luck or being cheeky, testing what you can get away with
the literal sense: put on a garment to check its size

explanation.surface: Advice to be bold, and to check a garment is the right size.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to chance one's arm cheekily and literally to put clothing on to test it.

clue.text: Musical lubricant?

definitions.meaning: a stage show and film set in 1950s America, starring John Travolta in the film
an oily substance smeared on machine parts

explanation.surface: A tuneful kind of oil.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a famous stage and film musical is also a thick oily lubricating substance.

clue.text: Cart jet bumpily over railway path

indicators.note: bumpily suggests a jolting ride that throws the letters out of order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A cart and a jet jolting along over a railway track.
explanation.definitionFit: The curved course followed by a projectile through the air is its route or line of travel.

clue.text: Excellent of French to provide assistant

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or excellent, with the 1 read as I
de is the French word for of

explanation.surface: An excellent French connection to supply a helper.
explanation.definitionFit: A helper or right-hand person is an assistant, often to an official or politician.

clue.text: 21 Across is drunk — socially acceptable — cheers!

indicators.note: is drunk suggests reeling about, so those letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: points to the answer at 21 Across, the helper
U means upper-class, so socially acceptable

explanation.surface: An assistant is tipsy but still respectable, and raises a toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is drunk' shuffles the 21 Across letters into ADIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A French farewell; cheers is informal British for goodbye, so both are parting words.

clue.text: Blow it! I may be stuck behind this big creature

indicators.note: stuck behind says the words before go after the piece that follows

parts.note: wap is an old word for a blow or strike
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry, 'Blow it!', from someone stuck behind a huge animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow it!' looks like an exclamation, but Blow gives WAP, and 'it! I' then sit behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A large North American deer, also called an elk, is a big creature.

clue.text: Terribly tiring backing Brussels plot

indicators.note: terribly says the letters of the next word are badly mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

indicators.note: backing means read the piece backwards

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the EU, the European Union

explanation.surface: An exhausting political scheme supported by Brussels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' turns TIRING into INTRIG, and 'backing' turns EU into UE.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret scheme or conspiracy is a plot.

clue.text: Main course served to Americans on board, it's said

indicators.note: it's said tells us the answer sounds like the phrase rather than being spelt like it

parts.note: on gives ON; a board here is a tray for carrying food

explanation.surface: A meal brought to American passengers on a plane or ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' looks like travel; it is 'on tray', which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US the word names the main dish of a meal, unlike its British starter sense.

clue.text: Supernatural being eating startled gnu: swallow completely

indicators.note: eating means the outer piece takes the other into itself

parts.note: an elf is a small supernatural being of folklore

indicators.note: startled suggests jumping about, so the letters of gnu are disturbed

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale creature devouring a frightened wildebeest whole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supernatural being' could be a ghost or god, but the three-letter elf is what fits around the jumbled antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: To overwhelm or envelop something entirely, as a flood or fire does, is to swallow it up.
